units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Yes, I'd like so terrible much to--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Stops in front of him.
Well; may I ask what you want?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, it was just this, your Reverence: we've been paid off down yonder--my grateful thanks to you, ma'am,--and now everything's finished, I've been thinking it would be but right and proper if we, that have been working so honestly together all this time--well, I was thinking we ought to end up with a little prayer-meeting to-night.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: A prayer-meeting? Down at the Orphanage?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, if your Reverence doesn't think it proper--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Oh yes, I do; but--h'm--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I've been in the habit of offering up a little prayer in the evenings, myself--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Have you?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, every now and then just a little edification, in a manner of speaking. But I'm a poor, common man, and have little enough gift, God help me!--and so I thought, as the Reverend Mr. Manders happened to be here, I'd--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Well, you see, Engstrand, I have a question to put to you first. Are you in the right frame of mind for such a meeting! Do you feel your conscience clear and at ease?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, God help us, your Reverence! we'd better not talk about conscience.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Yes, that is just what we must talk about. What have you to answer?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Why--a man's conscience--it can be bad enough now and then.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Ah, you admit that. Then perhaps you will make a clean breast of it, and tell me--the real truth about Regina?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Quickly.
Mr. Manders!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Reassuringly.
Please allow me--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: About Regina! Lord, what a turn you gave me!
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Looks at MRS. ALVING.
There's nothing wrong about Regina, is there?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: We will hope not. But I mean, what is the truth about you and Regina? You pass for her father, eh!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Uncertain.
Well--h'm--your Reverence knows all about me and poor Johanna.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Come now, no more prevarication! Your wife told Mrs. Alving the whole story before quitting her service.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, then, may--! Now, did she really?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: You see we know you now, Engstrand.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: And she swore and took her Bible oath--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Did she take her Bible oath?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: No; she only swore; but she did it that solemn-like.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: And you have hidden the truth from me all these years? Hidden it from me, who have trusted you without reserve, in everything.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, I can't deny it.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Have I deserved this of you, Engstrand? Have I not always been ready to help you in word and deed, so far as it lay in my power? Answer me. Have I not?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: It would have been a poor look-out for me many a time but for the Reverend Mr. Manders.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: And this is how you reward me! You cause me to enter falsehoods in the Church Register, and you withhold from me, year after year, the explanations you owed alike to me and to the truth. Your conduct has been wholly inexcusable, Engstrand; and from this time forward I have done with you!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: With a sigh.
Yes! I suppose there's no help for it.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: How can you possibly justify yourself?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Who could ever have thought she'd have gone and made bad worse by talking about it? Will your Reverence just fancy yourself in the same trouble as poor Johanna--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: I!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Lord bless you, I don't mean just exactly the same. But I mean, if your Reverence had anything to be ashamed of in the eyes of the world, as the saying goes. We menfolk oughtn't to judge a poor woman too hardly, your Reverence.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: I am not doing so. It is you I am reproaching.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Might I make so bold as to ask your Reverence a bit of a question?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Yes, if you want to.
units.name: MANDERS
